1 Year Ago...

I took the last week in December off for the holidays. Each night I got drunk and high. By the end of it, I was starting to get bags under my eyes, my voice was reminiscent of a homeless drunkard, and I could lift measurably less weight on returning to the gym.

So began Dry January 2018. I did it alone, and did not make any exceptions for alcohol use. Initially, I considered smoking marijuana as a fallback in case I really needed a buzz. However, a few days in I decided to stay completely sober on realizing that I had never spent more than 2 weeks sober since turning 21 all those years ago.

It can be, ironically, a psychedelic exploration of sobriety if you have never been sober for a good length of time in your adult life. You will feel better rested, have more mental clarity, time, and energy. I swear you can feel your body repairing itself you are a heavy drinker and take a break for a while. Challenges at work were no problem because I had the energy and mental clarity to handle them when they arose. I got much more reading done than usual. I worked through a personal finance book, and significantly organized by finances better. I gained a lot in terms of personal insight and reflection (make sure to write down your reflections and goals during this time).

One downside for me is that I did not grow my social or dating life that month, since alcohol is such a social lubricant. The 60 day NoBooze challenge that @Native is organizing allows a limited exception for social gatherings, so this doesn't become a problem for you.

Some signs you may be drinking too much are:

  • You feel anxious in social situations without a drink.

  • Your standing at work is affected because you show up hungover. You think you play it off like you are not hungover, but lack the energy to handle challenges properly at work.

  • You keep missing gym days because you are drunk/hungover.

  • You have a stack of unread books that you can never find the time to open, but somehow find the time to spend several nights per week drunk.

One of the biggest impacts of heavy drinking is that it saps your energy over time. Your hangover may heal in 1 day, but heavy drinking reduces your energy over the short/medium term through a number of mechanisms. Some of them are:

  • Reduced sleep quality. Source

  • Fewer red blood cells due to impaired production. Source

  • Lowered testosterone. Source

  • Oxidative damage to cells across the body. Source

  • Impaired wound/cell healing (that you now need). Source

  • Suppressed immune system. Source

  • Reduced neurogenesis (brain cell growth). Source

SAFETY NOTICE: If you have been drinking heavily every night for a month or more, you need to taper your alcohol consumption. Acute alcohol withdrawal can kill you and has been strongly correlated to serious long term ill effects, such as IQ decline. If this applies to you, research "tapering alcohol" which basically means if you have 10 drinks every night, have 8 tonight, then 6 the next night, then 4.... The mods of v/theredpill have been flexible with those who need to delay their challenge start dates. If you simply got drunk for the past 3 nights because it is the weekend/New Years, you do not need to taper.

I hope you'll give it a shot, if you need it. Happy New Year everyone!
